summary: George Uglow Pope was an Indologist and linguist. He headed Breeks Memorial School (1859-1870) and Bishop Cotton Boys' School (1870), both of which he founded, before serving as Lecturer in Tamil at the University of Oxford from 1883.

George V. Bobrinskoy was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franklin Edgerton at the Lutheran Theological Seminary, the University of Pennsylvania, and Yale. He taught at Yale (1927-1928) and was Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Chicago (1951-1967).

George Watt, an Indologist, studied at Aberdeen, Glasgow, and King's College London. He served as Professor of Botany at the University of Calcutta (1873) and Presidency University (1873-1874), later working at the Indian Museum, Kolkata (~1894-1906).

George Weston Briggs worked in Indology and religious studies after earning a B.S. at Northwestern University. His main appointments included Professor of English Literature at Lucknow Christian College (~1903-1910) and Professor of History of Religions at Drew University (1929-1944).

George William Brown specialized in Indology and religious studies, completing his Ph.D. under Maurice Bloomfield at Johns Hopkins. He served as Principal of Christian Bible College (~1903-1917) and Professor of Semitic Languages and Missions at Lexington Theological Seminary (1927-1932).

George de Roerich studied across London, Harvard, and Paris under scholars including Lanman, Lévi, and Pelliot. A specialist in Tibetology and Indology, he directed the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute (from 1928) and held posts at Moscow State University and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

George van Driem is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Virginia and Leiden University. He held the Chair for Descriptive Linguistics at Leiden (1996-2009) and the Chair of Historical Linguistics at the University of Bern (2010-2022).

Georges B. J. Dreyfus is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned a Geshe degree at Ganden Shartse Monastery and a doctorate under Jeffrey Hopkins at the University of Virginia, later becoming Jackson Professor of Religion at Williams College (~1992).

Georges Cuendet was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Charles Bally at Geneva and Antoine Meillet at the EPHE and INALCO. He served as Privatdozent of Indology at the University of Geneva from 1938 to 1963.

Georges Dandoy worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studying at Namur, Stonyhurst, Oxford, and St. Mary's College, Kurseong. He held teaching posts at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1909-1912), St. Mary's College, Kurseong (1917-1922), and the University of Calcutta.

Georges Dumézil studied under Antoine Meillet and Marcel Mauss in Paris. A scholar of religious studies and linguistics, he held posts at Istanbul, Uppsala, the EPHE (1935-1968), INALCO (1937-1948), and the Collège de France (1949-1968).
Georges Guieysse was an Indologist and linguist who studied in Paris under Sylvain Lévi, Michel Bréal, Abel Bergaigne, Ferdinand de Saussure, and James Darmesteter between 1886 and 1889.

Georges Perrot was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure. He later served on the faculty of the University of Paris (~1877-1904) and as director of the École Normale Supérieure (~1883-1904).

Georges Redard was a linguist who studied at Neuchâtel, Bern, Paris under Émile Benveniste, and Tehran. He was an associate professor at the University of Bern from 1954 and also taught at Neuchâtel, Lausanne, and the Collège de France.

Georges Strehly was an Indologist educated at the École Normale Supérieure, the Sorbonne, and the EPHE under Paul Regnaud and Abel Bergaigne. He taught at Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour (1879-1886) and Lycée Louis-le-Grand (1886-1906).

Georges-Jean Pinault is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the ENS, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and the EPHE under Jean Haudry. He was a professor at Blaise Pascal University (~1986-1996) and became Professor at the EPHE in 1999.

Georgij Aleksandrovič Zograf was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov and Vasilij Matveevič Beskrovnyj. From 1954, he worked as a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts.

Georgij Saridanovič Ahvlediani studied linguistics at Kharkiv under Friedrich Knauer and at Saint Petersburg under Carl Salemann and Fyodor Shcherbatskoy. He was Professor at Tbilisi State University from 1918 and directed the Institute of Linguistics of the Georgian Academy of Sciences (1949-1950).

Georgios Kozakis Typaldos studied medicine at the University of Padua and worked in the field of Indology. He served as Librarian at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens from approximately 1842 to 1863.

Georgios Nikolaou Hatzidakis was a linguist who studied at Athens, Leipzig, Jena, and Berlin under scholars including Windisch, Brugmann, and Delbrück. He served as Rector of Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (1926) and President of the Academy of Athens (1927).
